text:
devon: CI red on flaky unit: retry_manager_test::backoff_jitter_interleaving — failing ~1/20 on main, can't repro in presubmit. anyone seen this pattern recently?
sam: Can you paste the failing job id/log tail?
devon: job=2025-06-12_14:03, here's the last ~20 lines from the test run:
```
[ RUN      ] retry_manager_test/RandomJitter
thread 'main' panicked at 'assertion failed: retries == expected', runtime/src/retry/manager.rs:214
note: run with RUST_BACKTRACE=1 for a backtrace
--- stdout ---
attempts: [1, 2]
expected attempts: 3
--- end ---
```
maya: hmm could be timing nondeterminism around the jitter + scheduler. Did CI run on the new qemu hosts? env diff?
devon: CI matrix used linux-x86-64-2025-06. I can repro locally with stress: `./bazel test //runtime:retry_manager_test --runs_per_test=200 --test_arg=--stress`. hit a failure after ~37 runs on my local dev box.
linda: @sam maybe 9f3c2d6 (prefetch refactor) touched the same timer paths, worth bisecting.
sam: starting a bisect on the CI matrix now, also kicking a quick rerun. tagging @ci-bot to queue.
ci-bot: Rerun queued by sam for job 2025-06-12_14:03 (build 5821) — will post results.
maya: short-term mitigation: make the test deterministic by injecting a fixed RNG seed or remove reliance on wall-clock jitter. Longer-term we should harden the retry invariants so the test only checks state, not exact timing.
devon: I can open a tiny PR that injects a seed when TEST_DETERMINISTIC=1 and adds a harness to advance the fake timer. will attach failing run logs to the PR.
sam: cool — if bisect points to a specific commit I'll post it here and we can decide revert vs fix.
devon: thanks — I'll start the PR and paste the local repro steps + stacktrace. :thumbsup:
